reasoning_traces.think:
The core idea of regime-dependent causal discovery hinges on modeling dynamical systems that switch between persistent, unobserved background states, each with unique causal structures. The Regime-PCMCI algorithm alternates between estimating regime assignments and learning causal graphs within those regimes. This dual optimization approach allows for joint inference without prior knowledge of regimes. In the first step, PCMCI is applied to subsets of data defined by high-probability regime assignments (γ_k(t) ≥ 0.5), yielding causal graphs P_k and coefficients Φ_k. In the second step, these fixed graphs inform the regime assignment process by minimizing a cost functional L(Γ,P), which balances prediction accuracy and regime persistence. The persistence constraint ensures that regime switches are not overly frequent, modeled as a sum of absolute differences in regime indicators across time. The method assumes discrete, finite regimes and within-regime stationarity. It leverages synthetic and real-world datasets such as ENSO and All-India Rainfall to validate its ability to recover causal structures under changing conditions. The technique is particularly powerful for domains where causal mechanisms shift over time, such as climate dynamics or complex socio-economic systems.
